summary: Validated public API and complete mobile browser workflow: welcome, theme, seven languages, login, patient intake, seven-question assessment, simulator stream, three movement tests, result tabs, and report action all passed.

critical.issue: Assessment state is a single process-global dictionary and stop updates a patient by id without owner_id; concurrent clinicians could see or persist another user's assessment.

minor.issue: AssessmentInput does not validate that all seven questionnaire responses exist or that answer keys are limited to the seven questions; UI enforces this, but direct API callers can start incomplete assessments.

action_items: Scope assessment state to an authenticated user/session and enforce patient ownership on stop/update.
Validate exactly seven questionnaire responses at the assessment API boundary.
critical_code_review_comments: The in-memory global assessment_state is unsafe for multi-user clinical use and is not horizontally scalable.
seed_data_creation: Created one TEST_JointSense Patient via API and one Browser Test Patient via UI for assessment coverage.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Complete primary UI workflow passed at mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow. Re-test concurrent-user assessment isolation and direct API validation after fixes.
rca of the issue: Assessment lifecycle stores clinical data in module-level assessment_state and stop_assessment performs an unscoped patient update. This is a shared mutable state/authz boundary issue rather than a UI failure.
